questions.stem: Graphite is widely used as a dry lubricant in high-temperature machines. Which structural feature is primarily responsible for this property?

options.option_text: Each carbon is sp3 hybridized forming a rigid 3D tetrahedral network
Layers are held by weak van der Waals forces and slide over each other
Graphite contains delocalized electrons that reduce surface friction
Its high melting point prevents molecular breakdown under thermal stress

questions.explanation: B is correct because graphite has a layered hexagonal structure where adjacent layers are held only by weak van der Waals forces, allowing them to slide easily over one another — the basis of lubrication. Option C is a common confusion: delocalized electrons explain graphite's electrical conductivity, not its lubricating ability. Option A describes diamond's structure, which is the opposite of graphite.

questions.stem: Carbon monoxide is acutely toxic to humans even at low concentrations. What is the primary physiological mechanism behind its toxicity?

options.option_text: It reacts with stomach acid to form corrosive carbonic acid compounds
It binds to haemoglobin ~250 times more strongly than oxygen does
It inhibits the enzyme acetylcholinesterase in nerve synapses directly
It blocks insulin receptors in the pancreas reducing glucose metabolism

questions.explanation: B is correct because CO has an affinity for haemoglobin roughly 200–250 times that of O₂, forming stable carboxyhaemoglobin and preventing oxygen transport to tissues. Option C describes the mechanism of organophosphate nerve agents (e.g., sarin), a common mismatch candidates make. CO does not act on the gut or pancreas.

questions.stem: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) and dimethyl ether (CH₃OCH₃) both have the molecular formula C₂H₆O but display very different chemical behaviours. What category of isomerism do they represent?

options.option_text: Optical isomerism arising from a chiral carbon centre
Functional group isomerism with different chemical properties
Chain isomerism caused by different carbon skeleton arrangements
Geometrical isomerism due to restricted rotation around a bond

questions.explanation: B is correct: ethanol contains an –OH group while dimethyl ether contains a C–O–C linkage — the same molecular formula but different functional groups, which is functional group isomerism. Option C (chain isomerism) involves different carbon skeletons with the SAME functional group. Optical and geometrical isomerism require a chiral centre or a C=C double bond respectively, which are absent here.

questions.stem: During saponification, a vegetable oil (triglyceride) is hydrolysed with hot concentrated sodium hydroxide solution. Which two products are always formed?

options.option_text: Soap (sodium salt of fatty acid) and glycerol as a by-product
Soap (sodium salt of fatty acid) and ethanol as a by-product
Detergent (sulphonate salt) and water as the only by-product
Fatty acids and sodium carbonate as the two major products

questions.explanation: A is correct: saponification cleaves the ester bonds of a triglyceride — the three fatty acid chains leave as sodium salts (soap) and the glycerol backbone is released intact. Option B is wrong because ethanol is released only in ester hydrolysis of ethyl esters, not triglycerides. Option D is wrong because NaOH yields sodium salts (soaps), not free fatty acids; sodium carbonate is not produced.

questions.stem: Glacial acetic acid (pure ethanoic acid) boils at 118 °C whereas ethanol boils at only 78 °C, despite their molar masses being very close. What best explains this difference?

options.option_text: Ethanoic acid forms stable dimers through paired hydrogen bonds
Ethanol molecules have stronger London dispersion forces overall
Ethanoic acid is partially ionic, requiring extra energy to vaporise
Ethanol's lower surface tension reduces the energy needed to boil it

questions.explanation: A is correct: ethanoic acid molecules form cyclic dimers via two simultaneous hydrogen bonds (O–H···O=C), effectively doubling the intermolecular force and raising the boiling point markedly. Ethanol forms only single hydrogen bonds and has a lower boiling point as a result. Option B is wrong because London dispersion forces increase with molecular size/mass, and ethanol is the smaller molecule here; ethanoic acid is not ionic.

questions.stem: Buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀) is described as having the same geometry as a truncated icosahedron. How many pentagonal faces does the C₆₀ cage contain, and how many hexagonal faces?

options.option_text: 20 pentagonal faces arranged symmetrically across the sphere
12 pentagonal faces interspersed among 20 hexagonal faces
6 pentagonal faces at each of the 10 axial positions only
30 pentagonal faces alternating with 12 larger hexagonal faces

questions.explanation: B is correct: by Euler's theorem for closed polyhedra (V – E + F = 2) applied to a cage where every vertex is 3-connected, any fullerene must have exactly 12 pentagonal faces regardless of size; C₆₀ additionally has 20 hexagons, giving 60 vertices. Option A swaps the counts (20 pentagons is incorrect). Option D is entirely fabricated. No two pentagons in C₆₀ share an edge — a stability rule known as the isolated-pentagon rule.

questions.stem: Carbon-14 used in radiocarbon dating is produced when cosmic-ray neutrons strike atmospheric nitrogen-14 nuclei. Which statement correctly pairs the half-life of C-14 with the practical upper age limit of the technique?

options.option_text: Half-life ~5,730 years; reliably dates organic material up to ~50,000 years old
Half-life ~14,300 years; reliably dates organic material up to ~100,000 years old
Half-life ~5,730 years; reliably dates organic material up to ~500 years old
Half-life ~1,600 years; reliably dates organic material up to ~15,000 years old

questions.explanation: A is correct: C-14 has a half-life of 5,730 years (±40 years), and after ~8–9 half-lives (~50,000 years) the remaining C-14 activity falls below reliable detection limits. Option D confuses C-14 with Ra-226 (half-life ~1,600 years). Option C wrongly implies the technique is useless beyond 500 years — it is in fact the primary tool for archaeological samples in the 1,000–40,000 year range. Option B overstates both the half-life and the upper limit.
